question:
CuSO₄ + Mg → MgSO₄ + Cu

In the above reaction Mg is the:
solution:
The correct answer is** __reducing agent__**.

***__Key-points__**

__
 
• a reducing agent (also known as a reductant, reducer, or electron donor) is **a chemical species that "donate" an electron to an electron recipient** (called the oxidizing agent, oxidant, oxidizer, or electron acceptor).
 
• CuII + 2 e- → Cu0 (reduction)
 
• Mg0 - 2 e- → MgII (oxidation)
 
• Reduction is the gain of electrons or a reduction* in the oxidation state of an atom, ion, or certain atoms in a molecule.
 
• Mg + CuSO4 = Cu + MgSO4 is a redox reaction where Mg is oxidized and Cu is reduced.
 
• Mg is a** reducing agent (i.e. it lost electrons)** and CuSO4 is an oxidizing agent (i.e. it gained electrons).

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional information__**

 
• **Oxidizing agent**

 
 
• ​An oxidizing agent (often referred to as an oxidizer or an oxidant) is **a chemical species that tends to oxidize other substances**, i.e. cause an increase in the oxidation state of the substance by making it lose electrons.
 
 
 
• ​**Dissolving agent**
 
 
• ​**A solvent** is a dissolving agent and is the liquid portion of a solution.
 
• The molecules that** dissolve in the solvent **are called **solutes.**
 
 
 
• **​Catalyst**
 
 
• ​A catalyst is **a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction or lowers the temperature or pressure needed to start one, without itself being consumed during the reaction**.
 
• Catalysis is the process of adding a catalyst** to facilitate a reaction.**
